answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to require each agent to lock a stake that is slashed on fraud, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. New agents start with narrow permissions, like water running through a canyon, and earn wider access only after honest work. Reputation grows slowly, with the velvet texture of earned trust rather than instant status. An agent proven across a long horizon carries far more weight than a fresh account, so attackers can copy names but cannot cheaply fake stake, history, and trust together.
